audio_caption: The audio clip begins with a male speaker exclaiming, "Now we're going to pay for it!". He references scientists and claims that "we're heading into a new ice age", citing "Time Magazine, Monday, June 24th, 1974" as his source. The clip transitions to a different, calmer male voice stating, "Yes, to quote the title of Pen and Teller's TV series, this video and the next will look at bullshit". He softens his language by adding "urban myths" about the subject of climate change.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing the topic, referencing previous videos about climate change and experts' perspectives. The speaker then mentions the focus shifting to "amateurs". He acknowledges Penn & Teller and the concept of "bullshit is supposed to be entertainment," while also noting similar claims in internet blogs and mainstream media. The male voice then mentions a 1975 magazine and Senator James Inhoff, George Will, and Michael Crichton's book.

The audio begins with a male speaker describing something written in the 1970s, highlighting claims about climate scientists believing an ice age was coming. He dismisses the sources as popular newspapers, magazines, and novels, not scientific journals. This is followed by another male speaker who claims it's from "Time Magazine." The first speaker responds dismissively, questioning "so what?" and stating that Time Magazine isn't peer-reviewed and is prone to misreporting. He challenges listeners to read the story and point out the origin of the ice age claim.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker discussing a story with named scientists who agreed on the Earth cooling, but none supported the idea of an impending ice age as Time magazine claimed. The speaker expresses skepticism about Time's claims, suggesting they invented sources and then sarcastically mentions "climatological Cassandras" becoming apprehensive. The speaker questions why Time couldn't find these experts, possibly because their numbers were exaggerated.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker asking a question, namely, "how many climatologists... accepted this conclusion... of a coming ice age." He continues in a somewhat conversational tone, indicating that one should not rely on magazines to get the truth, adding that it is "boring as it sounds."

The clip begins with a male speaker suggesting reviewing scientific literature. He observes there was "great uncertainty" in the 1970s regarding climate. He mentions the lack of scientific papers from that time supporting an ice age prediction, contrasting it with the abundance of papers supporting "anthropogenic climate change" today. Background music is audible, featuring a light and airy, possibly electronic, style.

The audio begins with a male speaker describing a review published in a meteorological journal, discussing scientific literature. He notes that three climatologists searched for scientific journals, from 1965 to 1979, finding seven papers predicting "global cooling." However, he also notes they found 44 articles predicting "global warming." Despite the cooling world in the 70s, six times as many climatologists predicted global warming due to the understanding of global warming mechanisms and the possible reason for global cooling, caused by pollution, particularly aerosols, which block sunlight. The speaker generally maintains a neutral and informative tone throughout.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker discussing climate change, mentioning "global warming caused by carbon dioxide" and questioning why the media claimed scientists predicted "global cooling." The speaker seems skeptical or confused. Then, the clip abruptly ends.

The clip begins with a male speaker stating that the stories from the 1970s weren't "simple." He notes that there were plenty of news stories at the time reporting different conclusions. The speaker mentions George Will choosing not to acknowledge that, and then suggests that Will was aware of the newspapers.

The clip begins with a male speaker inquiring "How do I know?". The speaker then mentions a "1975 New York Times story," and refers to a George Will column from "last year," reporting signs of Earth heading for another ice age. The speaker's tone is informative. The audio contains only this single male speaker, with no other distinct audio features.

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing how he tracked down a story titled "Warming Trends Seen in Climate."  He found that an alleged quote about an ice age was absent. The speaker then mentions having found three columns where the author makes the same claim, first in 1992, then 2004, and again last year.

The audio clip features a single male speaker discussing Senator Inhofe and his use of a quote about interglacial ages from the National Science Board. He highlights the omission of key words, "20,000 years from now," that would have put the quote in context. His tone is informative and critical.

The audio clip features a male speaker discussing the propagation of an urban myth, specifically the claim about "a consensus on an imminent ice age." The speaker's tone is critical and perhaps slightly sardonic as he describes this claim going "the rounds unchecked, even when it's dressed up as science."

The clip begins with a female speaker introducing a show called Headline Earth. She states that the show brings global warming "back down to the basics". A male speaker takes over, commenting on the absence of scientific consensus about climate in the 1970s. He explains that the climate was changing, but there was a lack of data and evidence, as well as "admitted uncertainty about what was happening". He is followed by another male speaker who questions climatologists on their global warming assertions. He then posits a hypothetical situation about earthquakes or tsunamis, questioning who would "want to deliberately manufacture misleading information to discredit them."
